title: Sep 17 Results + Sep 18 Preview: Solid Contact, Room to Improve
summary: 5-4 on Sep 17 with strong favorites hitting. Tomorrow we're backing Burns in Cincy.

content.value:
## Sep 17 Recap: The Favorites Delivered

From a pitcher's perspective, yesterday was about respecting the arms with momentum. We went 5-4, hitting 55.6% on the day. Not dominant, but profitable. The model leaned into higher-probability plays, and three of our strongest picks—Astros, Padres, and Rays—all came through when it mattered.

## What Worked, What Didn't

The picks above 60% confidence went 4-1. That's what you want to see—when the model identifies a clear edge, it's cashing. The Astros at 63% was the strongest lean, and they delivered. Same story with the Padres in Coors and the Rays at home.

The misses? All coin flips. Brewers-Pirates at 52%, Dodgers-Reds at 50%, Phillies-Mets at 50%, Tigers-Sox at 51%—these were essentially pick'em games. When you're playing margins that tight, you're going to take some lumps. That's baseball.

## Sep 18 Preview: Cubs @ Reds—Backing the Young Arm

Tomorrow's top pick is the **Cincinnati Reds** at home against the Cubs. This one's sitting at 50% confidence, so we're essentially calling a toss-up with a slight edge to the Reds.

The matchup: **Clay Holmes** for Chicago versus **Chase Burns** for Cincinnati. Holmes has been stretched out from the bullpen into a starter's role—it's a tough transition, and the command typically lags behind. Burns, on the other hand, is a young power arm with swing-and-miss stuff. At home in Great American Ball Park, he's got the platoon advantage and the fresher arm.

content.sub: 50% win probability vs Cubs · Chase Burns vs Clay Holmes

content.value:
## Pitcher's Take: Trust the Starter with the Role

Holmes is a reliever by trade. Asking him to give you 5+ innings with consistent stuff is a different animal. His velocity plays in short bursts, but over multiple times through the order, hitters adjust. Burns is built to start—he's got a deeper arsenal and the conditioning to maintain his fastball late.

In a 50-50 game, I'm leaning toward the guy who's been preparing all season to pitch deep into games. That's Burns. The Reds' bullpen has been shaky, so they need length from their starter. I think they get it.

Let's keep building on yesterday's momentum. Ride the favorable matchups, and don't overthink the tight ones.
